content.theory:
Basic forms collect names and passwords; advanced forms collect **the right data in the right format**. HTML5 gives you a rich toolbox of input types and built-in validation attributes that prevent bad data from ever reaching your server — no JavaScript required.

### The right input type

The `type` attribute turns a plain text box into a purpose-built field. Each type triggers the correct mobile keyboard, validation rule, and formatting hint:

| type | Used for | Built-in behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | Email addresses | Requires `@` and a domain |
| `tel` | Phone numbers | Shows the dial pad on mobile |
| `number` | Numeric values | Spin buttons + `min`/`max` |
| `date` | Calendar dates | Date picker in most browsers |
| `url` | Website links | Requires a valid URL format |
| `color` | Colour picker | Browser colour palette |
| `range` | Sliders | Visual slider, ideal with an output |

```html
<input type="email" name="email" required>
<input type="number" name="age" min="16" max="99">
<input type="date" name="dob">
<input type="range" name="level" min="1" max="10" value="5">
<input type="color" name="theme">
```

### Selects, optgroups, and textareas

A dropdown is a `<select>` filled with `<option>`s, optionally grouped with `<optgroup label="...">`. Long free-form input belongs in a `<textarea>`, where **rows** and **cols** set the visible box (users can still type more than it shows).

```html
<select name="batch">
  <optgroup label="Undergraduate">
    <option value="btech">B.Tech</option>
    <option value="bsc">B.Sc</option>
  </optgroup>
  <optgroup label="Postgraduate">
    <option value="mtech">M.Tech</option>
  </optgroup>
</select>

<textarea name="bio" rows="4" cols="40"></textarea>
```

### Grouping with fieldset and legend

Related fields — like shipping address, or 'Which role are you targeting?' — belong in a `<fieldset>`, titled by a `<legend>`. Screen readers announce the legend before each control inside it, and visual users get a clean grouped box.

```html
<fieldset>
  <legend>Contact details</legend>
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input type="email" id="email" name="email" required>
</fieldset>
```

### Validation attributes

Native validation is declarative: `required` blocks empty submission, `min`/`max` bound numbers and dates, `minlength`/`maxlength` bound text length, and `pattern` matches a **regular expression**. Pair them with `name` (so the server receives the data) and a matching `<label for="id">` (so clicking the label focuses the field).

```html
<input type="text" name="roll" pattern="[A-Z]{2}\d{4}" title="Two letters then four digits">
```

### Placeholder is not a label

`placeholder` shows grey hint text that disappears on focus and vanishes entirely on some screens — never use it as a replacement for a real `<label>`. A placeholder should *supplement* a label, not stand in for it.

### Common mistakes

- Using `placeholder` instead of `<label>` — an accessibility failure
- Forgetting `name` — the browser validates fine, but the server receives nothing
- Using `type="text"` for emails and phones — you lose free validation and mobile keyboards
- Applying `pattern` without a `title` hint — users do not know what format is expected
- `min`/`max` on a `<textarea>` — they do nothing; use `minlength`/`maxlength`

codeSnippets.code:
<form action="/api/signup" method="post">
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Registration</legend>

    <label for="email">Email</label>
    <input type="email" id="email" name="email" required>

    <label for="course">Course</label>
    <select id="course" name="course">
      <option value="btech">B.Tech</option>
      <option value="mtech">M.Tech</option>
    </select>

    <label for="notes">Notes</label>
    <textarea id="notes" name="notes" rows="4" cols="40"></textarea>
  </fieldset>
  <button type="submit">Register</button>
</form>
codeSnippets.output: A grouped registration form with a required email field, a course dropdown, and a textarea.

exercise.instruction: Build a <form> containing a <fieldset> with a <legend> reading 'Registration'. Inside it, add: a <select> named 'course' with at least two <option>s, a <textarea> named 'notes' with rows and cols, and an email input named 'email' marked required. Close the fieldset and the form.
hints: Hint 1: Wrap everything in <fieldset> and add <legend>Registration</legend>.
Hint 2: Add <select name="course"> with two <option>s, and a <textarea name="notes" rows="4" cols="40">.
Hint 3: Finish with a required email input: <input type="email" name="email" required>.
